data.name: Rudrika
data.gender_notes: Rudrika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Woman who delights in the Rudra God
data.long_meaning: Woman who delights in the Rudra God (Shiva) In Hindu mythology, Rudra is the god of destruction and the lord of the cremation ground. This name is derived from the word 'Rud' which means roar, and the suffix 'ka' which means 'the one who'. Thus, the name Rudrika signifies a woman who is devoted to Rudra or Lord Shiva. The name Rudrika carries the meaning “Woman who delights in the Rudra God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Rudrika usually hope their child will grow to embody woman who delights in the rudra god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Devotion to Lord Shiva, destruction and transformation, creativity and expression
data.etymology: Rudrika belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Woman who delights in the Rudra God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rudrika total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Rudra, the god of primal energy and terror, was often invoked by name as Rudra-Rudhra, Rudraka or Rudrika during Vedic rituals. These names were also used during the Shiva Purana and the Mahabharata, indicating a continuity of use in Hindu tradition from the Vedic period to the medieval era.
historical_references.time_period: Vedic (c. 1500–500 BCE) to medieval (c. 6th-13th century CE)

historical_references.reference: Rudraka was also a surname used by the Vedic Brahmin families. The Rudrakas mentioned in the Rigveda were likely the priests responsible for invoking and appeasing the god Rudra during Vedic rituals. In later Hindu texts, the name Rudraka is also used to refer to Shiva, further emphasizing the continuity of Rudra with Shiva as the god of primal energy and destruction.

trends: Goddess of fertility and childbirth, Rudra (Shiva's wife) is known as Rudrika. In modern times, Rudrika is revered as a symbol of fertility and prosperity.
platforms: Instagram: Many Hindu communities post pictures of Rudrika idols, rituals, and offerings during the Navratri festival when Rudrika is worshipped.
Twitter: Hashtags like #RudrikaWorship and #RudrikaPuja are used to share images and stories related to the deity and her worship.
YouTube: Videos of Rudrika Puja, a ritual dedicated to the goddess, are popular during Navratri. These videos offer instructions and guidance on performing the Puja at home.
modern_usage.modern_context: In modern Hindu culture, Rudrika is revered as a symbol of fertility and prosperity. She is primarily worshipped during Navratri, a nine-day festival dedicated to the worship of nine forms of the divine feminine. During this time, Hindus decorate and offer prayers to Rudrika idols, perform special rituals, and seek her blessings for a healthy and prosperous life.
